sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Broad sector breadth remains narrow with only 2 of 11 sectors all-green, anchored by dominant strength in Energy and Technology alongside a rotation into Consumer Defensive.

Energy continues to lead the market with a commanding momentum score of 0.933 (rank 1), joined by Technology (0.717 momentum, rank 2) at the top of the performance table. Breadth is constrained, as only Energy and Communication Services maintain positive returns across all timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD).

Rotational pressure is evident beneath the surface. Defensive positioning saw Consumer Defensive jump +2 spots over the past 5 sessions to rank 6, while Healthcare faded, slipping -2 spots to rank 7 despite carrying a relatively high momentum score. Laggards remain anchored at the bottom, with Utilities plumbing the absolute lows at a momentum score of 0.067.

## Strength
- Energy dominates market leadership, ranking 1st YTD with an unmatched 0.933 momentum score and an unblemished all-green profile across all timeframes.
- Technology holds firm as the second-strongest sector, posting a 0.717 momentum score and maintaining its rank 2 standing.
- Overall market breadth is narrow, with only 2 of 11 groups (Energy and Communication Services) registering all-green across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD periods.

## Movers & Momentum
- Consumer Defensive posted the largest 5-day improvement, advancing +2 spots to rank 6 with a momentum score of 0.417.
- Financial and Communication Services each gained +1 spot over the last 5 sessions, reaching momentum scores of 0.683 (rank 5) and 0.617 (rank 9), respectively.
- Utilities sits as the primary momentum laggard at 0.067 (rank 10, -1 spot in 5 days), closely followed by Consumer Cyclical (0.283 momentum, rank 11) and Real Estate (0.283 momentum, rank 8).

## Divergences
- Healthcare exhibits clear fading behavior, dropping -2 spots over the last 5 sessions to rank 7 despite retaining an elevated 0.633 momentum score.
- Industrials shows an internal disconnect, holding an upper-tier YTD rank of 4 despite carrying a weak 0.300 momentum score.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and marine shipping remain the dominant market pillars, while commodity extractors and select healthcare groups are experiencing sharp short-term rank declines.

Market leadership remains heavily concentrated, with only 11 of 144 groups holding all-green status across all timeframes. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.980) and Marine Shipping (momentum 0.937) anchor sustained strength, while Consumer Electronics shows accelerating power by jumping 16 spots to rank 28 alongside a 0.921 momentum score. Defensive and communication pockets are also rotating higher, led by Internet Content & Information (+21 spots to rank 69) and Tobacco (+18 spots to rank 40).

Conversely, basic materials and mining are fading fast, highlighted by steep 5-session drops in Coking Coal (-34 spots to rank 83), Uranium (-26 spots to rank 101), and Aluminum (-19 spots to rank 88). Deterioration is also hitting groups with previously strong profiles, such as Biotechnology, which fell 18 spots despite sustained higher-timeframe metrics. Meanwhile, defensive retail is quietly turning up from low momentum bases.

## Strength
- **Pervasive Energy Leadership:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing leads the entire market (momentum 0.980, rank 2), supported by Oil & Gas Integrated (momentum 0.889, rank 8) and Oil & Gas E&P (momentum 0.844, rank 11), all maintaining all-green profiles.
- **Top-Tier Resiliency:** Marine Shipping (momentum 0.937, rank 4) and Financial Conglomerates (momentum 0.84) continue to hold sustained top-36 rankings across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
- **Narrow Breadth:** High-level strength remains tight across the broader market, with just 11 of 144 industry groups positive across the week, month, quarter, half-year, and year-to-date.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Rapid Climbers:** Internet Content & Information posted the largest short-term advance (+21 spots to rank 69, momentum 0.74), followed by Tobacco (+18 spots to rank 40, momentum 0.73) and Consumer Electronics (+16 spots to rank 28, momentum 0.92).
- **Severe De-risking in Mining:** Coking Coal tumbled 34 spots to rank 83, Uranium plunged 26 spots to rank 101 (momentum 0.24), and Other Precious Metals & Mining dropped 21 spots to rank 99.
- **Bottom Laggards:** Footwear & Accessories anchors the bottom of the market (momentum 0.058, rank 142), flanked by Building Materials (momentum 0.124, rank 133) and Airports & Air Services (momentum 0.124, rank 140).

## Divergences
- **Fading Momentum:** Despite elevated medium-term scores, Biotechnology (momentum 0.72) plunged 18 spots over the last 5 sessions, while Business Equipment & Supplies (momentum 0.64) shed 22 spots to rank 51.
- **Healthcare & Silver Cracks:** Health Information Services (momentum 0.74) slipped 7 spots, and Silver (momentum 0.64) fell 6 spots, signaling potential distribution beneath strong absolute momentum scores.
- **Emerging Low-Base Rebounds:** Discount Stores gained 13 spots over 5 days despite weak 0.45 momentum, while Grocery Stores climbed 11 spots with a 0.40 momentum score, marking early rotation into defensive staples.
